# Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/README.md

<div align="center">
  <img src="./assets/ConoHaVPS_logo.png" title="ConoHa VPS" height="150" />
</div>

# Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider

- Terraform ウェブサイト: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform
- ドキュメント: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/gmo-internet/conohavps/latest/docs

Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider は、Terraform が [ConoHa VPS](https://vps.conoha.jp/) 上のリソースを管理できるようにするプラグインです。

現在、下記リソースの管理に対応しています。

- サーバー
- SSHキーペア
- ボリューム
- セキュリティグループ
- セキュリティグループルール

詳細については、ドキュメントを参照してください。

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider は、APIユーザーの認証情報を使用します。APIユーザーの作成については、[APIユーザーを作成する](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3/api-cp-vps3/cp-create_api_user-v3/) を参照してください。

> [!WARNING]
>  本ソフトウェアは現在ベータ版です。機能や動作が予告なく変更される場合があります。本番環境での使用前には十分なテストを行ってください。このベータ版 Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider を使用することで、これらの条件に同意したものとみなされます。

## 使用例

ドキュメントを参照してください。

> [!IMPORTANT]
> 本ソフトウェアは現在ベータ版につきデータソースは提供しておりません。リソースの作成に必要なパラメータについては [公開API(ConoHa VPS Ver.3.0)](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3) より取得ください。

## 要件

- [Terraform](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/install) >= 1.0
- [Go](https://go.dev/doc/install) >= 1.24

## 開発

### ビルド

ビルドには Go のインストールが必要になります。

Go のインストールが確認できたら、`make build` を実行します。

```
$ make build
```
### テスト

下記の環境変数の設定が必要です。各変数の詳細については、ドキュメントを参照してください。

- `CONOHAVPS_USER_ID`
- `CONOHAVPS_PASSWORD`
- `CONOHAVPS_TENANT_ID`
- `CONOHAVPS_REGION`
- `CONOHAVPS_IDENTITY_ENDPOINT`

環境変数が設定できたら、`make testacc` を実行します。

```
$ make testacc
```

> [!CAUTION]
> テストでは、ConoHa VPS 上に実際にリソースを作成するので、料金が発生することに注意してください。

# ConoHa VPS Provider

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/index.md

page_title: "ConoHa VPS Provider"
  The ConoHa VPS provider is used to interact with the resources supported by the ConoHa VPS via the ConoHa VPS public APIs.

# ConoHa VPS Provider

The ConoHa VPS provider is used to interact with the resources supported by the [ConoHa VPS](https://vps.conoha.jp/) via the [ConoHa VPS public APIs](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3/).

!> The ConoHa VPS provider is only supported ConoHa VPS(Ver.3.0). Cannot be used for ConoHa VPS(Ver.2.0).

-> Currently in beta, data sources are not provided. Please obtain the parameters required for resource creation from the [ConoHa VPS public APIs](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3/).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    conohavps = {
      source = "gmo-internet/conohavps"
    }
  }
}

# Configure the ConoHa VPS provider
provider "conohavps" {
  identity_endpoint = "Your identity endpoint"
  password          = "Your password"
  region            = "Your region"
  tenant_id         = "Your tenant ID"
  user_id           = "Your user ID"
}
```

## Configuration

-> Please create a public API user in advance. See the [create API user documentation](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3/api-cp-vps3/cp-create_api_user-v3/) .

!> Please exercise extreme caution when managing the provider configuration that contain authentication information.

The ConoHa VPS provider accepts two configuration sources.
If both are provided, the environment variable is used.

- Parameters in the provider configuration
- Environment variables

## Schema

### Optional

- `identity_endpoint` (String) The identity endpoint of ConoHa VPS Public API. The default value is `https://identity.c3j1.conoha.io/v3`. Can also be set with the `CONOHAVPS_IDENTITY_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the ConoHa VPS Public API. Can also be set with the `CONOHAVPS_PASSWORD` environment variable.
- `region` (String) The region of ConoHa VPS. The default value is `c3j1`. Can also be set with the `CONOHAVPS_REGION` environment variable.
- `tenant_id` (String) The Tenant ID of the ConoHa VPS Public API. Can also be set with the `CONOHAVPS_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `user_id` (String) The user ID of the ConoHa VPS Public API. Can also be set with the `CONOHAVPS_USER_ID` environment variable.

---

# conohavps_instance (Resource)

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/resources/instance.md

page_title: "conohavps_instance Resource - terraform-provider-conohavps"
subcategory: "Compute"
  Manages instance resource.

# conohavps_instance (Resource)

Manages instance resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Instance creation with attached volume, security group, and keypair
resource "conohavps_instance" "test" {
  instance_name_tag = "test-instance" # Instance name tag
  admin_pass        = "xxxxxxxxxxxx" # Admin password for the instance
  flavor_id         = "f2a77529-1815-43a2-bc14-1f3f6b09079c" # Flavor ID for the instance
  block_device =  [
    {
      uuid = conohavps_volume.test.id # Volume ID to attach
    }
  ]
  security_group = [
    {
      name = conohavps_securitygroup.test.name # Security group name
    },
  ]
  key_name = conohavps_keypair.test.name # Keypair name
  power_state = "<ACTIVE or SHUTOFF>" # Desired power state of the instance
}

# Volume creation
resource "conohavps_volume" "test" {
  size      = 200 # Size in GB
  image_ref = "884c1899-fefe-40bd-aab8-1001b1d9c895" # image UUID for boot volume
  description = "Test boot volume from image" # Volume description if needed
  name      = "test-boot-volume" # Volume name
  volume_type = "c3j1-ds02-boot" # Volume type
}

# keypair creation
resource "conohavps_keypair" "test" {
  name = "keypair_test" # Keypair name
  public_key = "ssh-rsa xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx..." # Replace with your actual public key
}

# security group creation
resource "conohavps_securitygroup" "test" {
  name        = "security_group_test" # Security group name
  description = "Test security group" # Security group description if needed
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `block_device` (Attributes List) The block device mapping for the instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--block_device))
- `flavor_id` (String) The UUID of the flavor. The flavor ID can be obtained from the [ConoHa v3 API](https://doc.conoha.jp/reference/api-vps3/api-compute-vps3/compute-get_flavors_list-v3/?btn_id=reference-compute-get_flavors_detail-v3--sidebar_reference-compute-get_flavors_list-v3). Changing this value will resize the instance.
- `instance_name_tag` (String) The name tag of the instance. Must be 1-255 characters long and contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). Changing this value will update the instance metadata.

### Optional

- `admin_pass` (String, Sensitive) The administrator password for the instance. If not provided, a random password will be generated by the API. The password must be 9-70 characters long and include at least one uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, and symbol. Changing this value will force the instance to be recreated.
- `key_name` (String) The name of the SSH key pair. Changing this value will force the instance to be recreated.
- `power_state` (String) The power state of the instance. Valid values are `ACTIVE` or `SHUTOFF`. The instance will be started or stopped to match this state when specified.
- `security_group` (Attributes List) The security groups to associate with the instance. Changing this value will update the instance's security groups. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--security_group))
- `user_data` (String) The user data to be made available to the instance. Must be a `base64-encoded string`. Changing this value will force the instance to be recreated.

### Read-Only

- `addresses` (Map of List of Object) The network addresses assigned to the instance.
- `id` (String) The UUID of the instance.
- `status` (String) The current status of the instance.

<a id="nestedatt--block_device"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block_device`

Required:

- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the volume to attach as a block device.

<a id="nestedatt--security_group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `security_group`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name of the security group.

## Import

Instances can be imported using its `id` .

```shell
$ terraform import conohavps_instance.instance_1 {{instance_uuid}}
```

---

# conohavps_keypair (Resource)

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/resources/keypair.md

page_title: "conohavps_keypair Resource - terraform-provider-conohavps"
subcategory: "Compute"
  Manages keypair resource.

# conohavps_keypair (Resource)

Manages keypair resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# keypair creation basic
resource "conohavps_keypair" "test" {
  name = "keypair_1" # keypair name
}
# keypair creation with provided public key
resource "conohavps_keypair" "with_public_key" {
  name = "keypair_2" # keypair name
  public_key = "ssh-rsa xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx..." # Replace with your actual public key
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the keypair. Must be 1-255 characters long and contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). Changing this value will force the keypair to be recreated.

### Optional

- `public_key` (String) The public key material. If not provided, a new keypair will be generated and the private key will be returned. Changing this value will force the keypair to be recreated.

### Read-Only

- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The private key material. This is only returned when a new keypair is generated (i.e., when public_key is not provided during creation).

## Import

Keypairs can be imported using its `name` .

```shell
$ terraform import conohavps_keypair.keypair_1 {{keypair_name}}
```

---

# conohavps_securitygroup (Resource)

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/resources/securitygroup.md

page_title: "conohavps_securitygroup Resource - terraform-provider-conohavps"
subcategory: "Network"
  Manages security group resource.

# conohavps_securitygroup (Resource)

Manages security group resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "conohavps_securitygroup" "group_1" {
  name = "tf-example-security-group-1"
}

resource "conohavps_securitygroup" "group_2" {
  name        = "tf-example-security-group-2"
  description = "this is description example"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the security group. The name length needs to be between 1 and 255. Changing this value will update the name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description of the security group. The description length needs to be between 0 and 255. Changing this value will update the description.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the security group.

## Import

Security group can be imported using its `id` .

For example:

```shell
$ terraform import conohavps_securitygroup.group_1 {{securitygroup_id}}
```

---

# conohavps_securitygroup_rule (Resource)

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/resources/securitygroup_rule.md

page_title: "conohavps_securitygroup_rule Resource - terraform-provider-conohavps"
subcategory: "Network"
  Manages security group rule resource.

# conohavps_securitygroup_rule (Resource)

Manages security group rule resource.

~> To expose all ports (1-65535), set `port_range_min` and `port_range_max` to `0`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "conohavps_securitygroup" "group_1" {
  name = "tf-example-security-group-1"
}

resource "conohavps_securitygroup" "group_2" {
  name = "tf-example-security-group-2"
}

# Expose all ports (1-65535)
resource "conohavps_securitygroup_rule" "rule_1" {
  securitygroup_id = resource.conohavps_securitygroup.group_1.id
  direction        = "ingress"
  ethertype        = "IPv4"
  protocol         = "tcp"
  port_range_min   = 0
  port_range_max   = 0
}

# Expose a specific port range
resource "conohavps_securitygroup_rule" "rule_2" {
  securitygroup_id = resource.conohavps_securitygroup.group_2.id
  direction        = "ingress"
  ethertype        = "IPv4"
  protocol         = "tcp"
  port_range_min   = 80
  port_range_max   = 8080
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `direction` (String) The direction of the security group rule. Valid values are `egress` or `ingress` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `ethertype` (String) The layer 3 protocol type. Valid values are `IPv4` or `IPv6` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `securitygroup_id` (String) The security group ID to which the security group rule belongs. Changing this value will create a new security group rule.

### Optional

- `port_range_max` (Number) The higher part of the allowed port range. If omitted, accepts any port or any ICMP type. When the protocol is `tcp` or `udp` , valid value needs to be between `1` and `65535` . When the protocol is `icmp`, valid value needs to be between `0` and `255` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `port_range_min` (Number) The lower part of the allowed port range. If omitted, accepts any port or any ICMP type. When the protocol is `tcp` or `udp` , valid value needs to be between `1` and `65535` . When the protocol is `icmp`, valid value needs to be between `0` and `255` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `protocol` (String) The layer 4 protocol type. Valid values are `tcp` or `udp` or `icmp` . If omitted, accepts any protocol. When specifying this option, a port range needs to be specified. Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `remote_group_id` (String) The ID of remote group. The value needs to be the security group ID. This option is mutually exclusive with `remote_ip_prefix` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.
- `remote_ip_prefix` (String) The remote CIDR. The value needs to be a valid CIDR. This option is mutually exclusive with `remote_group_id` . Changing this value will create a new security group rule.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the security group rule.

## Import

Security group rule can be imported using its `id` .

For example:

```shell
$ terraform import conohavps_securitygroup_rule.rule_1 {{securitygroup_rule_id}}
```

---

# conohavps_volume (Resource)

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/docs/resources/volume.md

page_title: "conohavps_volume Resource - terraform-provider-conohavps"
subcategory: "Volume"
  Manages volume resource.

# conohavps_volume (Resource)

Manages volume resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Add volume: Create an add volume
resource "conohavps_volume" "add_volume" {
  name        = "example-add-volume"
  size        = 200
  volume_type = "c3j1-ds02-add"
  description = "Example add volume"
}

# Boot volume: Create from an image
resource "conohavps_volume" "boot_volume" {
  name        = "example-boot-volume"
  size        = 100
  volume_type = "c3j1-ds02-boot"
  image_ref   = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111" # Replace with your saved image ID
  description = "Boot volume from image"
}

# Add volume: Create from saved image
resource "conohavps_volume" "add_volume_from_image" {
  name        = "example-image-volume"
  size        = 200
  volume_type = "c3j1-ds02-add"
  image_ref   = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111" # Replace with your saved image ID
  description = "Volume from saved image"
}

# Clone: Create a volume from an existing volume
resource "conohavps_volume" "cloned_volume" {
  name         = "example-cloned-volume"
  size         = conohavps_volume.add_volume.size
  volume_type  = conohavps_volume.add_volume.volume_type
  source_volid = conohavps_volume.add_volume.id
  description  = "Cloned from volume"
}

# Restore: Create a volume from a backup
resource "conohavps_volume" "restored_volume" {
  name        = "example-restored-volume"
  size        = 100 # Size must be equal to or greater than the backup source
  volume_type = "c3j1-ds02-boot"
  backup_id   = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111" # Replace with your backup ID
  description = "Restored from backup"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Volume name.
- `size` (Number) Volume size in GB. Allowed values: 30, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000.

### Optional

- `backup_id` (String) Backup ID to restore from.
- `description` (String) Volume description.
- `image_ref` (String) Image ID to create volume from.
- `source_volid` (String) Source Volume ID to clone from.
- `volume_type` (String) Volume type. Allowed values: c3j1-ds02-boot, c3j1-ds02-add.

### Read-Only

- `bootable` (String) Whether the volume is bootable.
- `id` (String) Volume ID.
- `status` (String) Volume status.

## Import

Volume can be imported using its `id` .

```shell
$ terraform import conohavps_volume.volume_1 {{volume_uuid}}
```

# セキュリティポリシー

Source: https://github.com/gmo-internet/terraform-provider-conohavps/blob/main/SECURITY.md

# セキュリティポリシー

## セキュリティ脆弱性の報告

Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider に関する脆弱性を発見された場合は、責任ある開示の原則（Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure, CVD）に従いご報告ください。内容を確認のうえ、適切にパッチを適用し、リリースノートで周知します。

## 脆弱性の報告方法

メールにてご連絡ください。

* **宛先** : [vuln-report@conoha.jp](mailto:vuln-report@conoha.jp)
* **件名** : `[SECURITY] Terraform ConoHa VPS Provider 脆弱性報告`
* **本文** : 後述する「報告に含めていただきたい情報」を可能な限り詳細にご記載ください。

**注記**  
報告を確認し次第、適切に対応します。受領確認や進捗連絡は原則行いませんが、必要に応じてご連絡いたします。

## 報告に含めていただきたい情報

- 再現手順または概念実証
- 使用した関連ツール（バージョン情報を含む）
- ツールの出力結果

**機密保持**  
報告内容および関連情報は、修正版がリリースされるまで機密情報として取り扱います。
報告者の皆様には、責任ある開示にご協力いただきますようお願いいたします。

---
